title: Nothing outside a run can learn that it finished: a worker signal, a push stream, a slow poll and a deadline
description:
Nothing outside a run can find out that it finished. The only options today are
guessing an interval or watching a file, and both were used badly in this epic —
by a worker and by the orchestrator.

## What actually happened

- Tick to1's worker drove a real `ticfac run-epic` in the background and then
  ran `sleep 300` in a loop, three times at least: 15 minutes of blind waiting
  for runs that may have finished in seconds. It had nothing better to wait on.
- The orchestrator (me) looked stalled repeatedly for the same reason, and
  three separate hand-rolled watchers were wrong: one keyed on a log file being
  non-empty and fired on a protocol warning, one matched a process name the
  agent does not carry, one expired at its own timeout while the work ran on.
- `tk herd wait` worked correctly when finally used — one agent.list, then ONE
  events.subscribe stream, no polling, per-agent wait times. But its own
  documentation is explicit: "A settled worker means 'worth looking now', never
  'the work is finished'." Observed exactly: it reported three agents settled
  while two had zero commits and no report.

## The five-minute number is NOT laziness

`DefaultPollInterval = 5 * time.Minute` (internal/reconcile/reconcile.go:33) is
deliberately WELL under `DefaultWipeThreshold = 20 * time.Minute`, and the
comment says why: "what makes the poll a keepalive rather than a status check".
On a substrate that takes an unaddressed job away, the beat IS the point.

That is correct for the cloud and wrong for a local herdr run, where nothing
wipes and a push stream exists. So the FIRST thing this tick decides: the
interval belongs to the EXECUTOR, not to one global constant. Local subprocess
and local herdr want seconds; a cloud sandbox wants the slow beat.

## The design: four layers, each covering the one above it failing

1. TRUTH IS DURABLE EVIDENCE. Commits on the attempt branch plus the report with
   its STATUS line. Never the agent's state. This is already the epic's own rule
   (tick 2xu) and it is what makes the same tick settle identically on either
   executor. Everything below is only a hint about WHEN TO LOOK.
2. A WORKER SIGNAL, as the primary wake-up. Low latency, no cost. Caveat, and it
   is this codebase's own rule: a record written by the thing that may be gone is
   not evidence of its liveness. So the signal wakes; the evidence decides. A
   lost signal is then harmless.
3. A PUSH STREAM where the substrate has one. herdr does, and it works. It
   cannot be the only mechanism: it fires on agent-idle, which is not
   completion, and a stream can break.
4. A SLOW POLL as the floor, and a DEADLINE above everything. The poll catches
   the lost signal and the dead stream; the deadline is the only thing that can
   speak about a job that will never finish. The reconciler already has both.

## What to build

- Emit a run event stream a non-participant can subscribe to — the backlog's
  run feed (ticfac tick n0r), which the operator proposed for dashboards and
  which is now independently motivated by a worker and an orchestrator both
  waiting badly. One append-only JSONL per run, run/tick/attempt identity on
  every line, versioned in the contract bundle.
- Make the poll interval executor-supplied, with the keepalive reasoning kept
  where the cloud needs it.
- Give WORKERS the guidance that corrected the orchestrator: never a blind
  sleep; wait on a condition. Neither profiles/implement-tick.md nor
  .tick/learnings.md says anything about waiting today. That gap is why a
  worker burned 15 minutes.

acceptance_criteria: A non-participant can subscribe to a run's events and learn of completion without polling a file or guessing an interval; the feed is append-only, carries run/tick/attempt identity on every line, and is versioned in the contract bundle. The poll interval is supplied by the executor rather than one global constant, and the keepalive reasoning survives where a cloud substrate needs it. Completion is still decided by durable evidence — commits plus the report — and a test proves a lost or late signal changes no verdict. Workers are told not to blind-sleep: the implement prompt and .tick/learnings.md both carry the rule, with the condition-wait shape spelled out. make test-short green.
